package_info.package_manager: N/A (malicious file delivered via email or web download)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (affects Windows systems with Microsoft Support Diagnostic Tool)
package_info.why_malicious: The malicious .diagcab file exploits a zero-day path traversal vulnerability in the Microsoft Support Diagnostic Tool (MSDT), enabling attackers to copy a malicious executable into the Windows Startup folder. This results in arbitrary code execution with user privileges upon the next system boot, establishing persistence and allowing malware installation without user consent.

execution_context.trigger: When a user opens the malicious .diagcab file (runtime via MSDT invocation)
execution_context.file_location: Maliciously crafted .diagcab file delivered via email attachment or web download
required_permissions: Write access to the user's Windows Startup folder
Ability to execute MSDT with user privileges
Filesystem access to AppData\Local\Temp and Startup directories

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
A .diagcab file containing a path traversal payload that copies a malicious executable to the Windows Startup folder, e.g.,

<CommandLine>copy ..\..\..\..\..\..\..\..\AppData\Local\Temp\malware.exe C:\Users\<username>\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\malware.exe</CommandLine>
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user opens the malicious .diagcab file, MSDT executes a command that abuses path traversal to copy a malicious executable from a temporary directory to the Windows Startup folder, resulting in the malware being automatically executed with user privileges on the next system boot.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The .diagcab file is intentionally crafted to exploit a path traversal vulnerability in MSDT, allowing unauthorized file writes to the Windows Startup folder. This technique is commonly used to establish persistence and bypass normal security controls.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate .diagcab files are intended for diagnostics and troubleshooting, typically reading or writing only to temporary or user-approved locations. They should never write executables to the Startup folder or use path traversal to access directories outside their intended scope.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate .diagcab files may copy diagnostic logs or scripts to temporary folders for troubleshooting, but they do not copy executables to autorun locations or use path traversal in file operations.
key_indicators: Presence of path traversal sequences (e.g., ..\..\) in <CommandLine> elements within .diagcab files
Copy operations targeting the Windows Startup folder (C:\Users\<username>\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\)
Executable payloads embedded within or referenced by the .diagcab archive
MSDT or its child processes performing file writes to autorun locations after opening a .diagcab file

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a malicious .diagcab file containing a path traversal payload designed to copy a malicious executable to the Windows Startup folder.
attack_chain.leads_to: User receives the malicious .diagcab file via email or web download.

attack_chain.action: User opens the malicious .diagcab file, causing MSDT to process the payload and execute the copy command, placing the malware in the Startup folder.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious executable is written to the Startup folder, set to run at next login or system boot.

attack_chain.action: On the next system boot or user login, Windows automatically executes the malware from the Startup folder, granting the attacker code execution and persistence.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker achieves persistent arbitrary code execution on the victim's system.

behavioral_signatures: Execution of MSDT with .diagcab files containing path traversal sequences in <CommandLine> elements
MSDT or its child processes performing unexpected file writes to the Windows Startup folder
Creation of new executable files in the Startup folder immediately following the opening of a .diagcab file
Unusual invocation of copy commands referencing AppData\Local\Temp and Startup directories within MSDT context
file_indicators: Presence of .diagcab files with embedded path traversal (..\..\) in command payloads
Temporary files in AppData\Local\Temp\ that are referenced by .diagcab payloads
Autorun entries or new files in Startup folder created shortly after .diagcab file activity
network_indicators: N/A (primary attack is local file system exploitation; any network activity would be due to secondary payloads post-execution)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for .diagcab files containing suspicious <CommandLine> payloads with path traversal sequences. Alert on any MSDT or child process writing executables to the Windows Startup folder. Correlate user activity logs with the opening of .diagcab files and subsequent creation of new autorun entries or executables in Startup. Employ endpoint protection to block or sandbox .diagcab files from untrusted sources, and flag any copy operations from temporary directories to autorun locations.
